segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus was inside a packed house, teaching, when word came in from the edge of the crowd.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His mother and his brothers were standing outside, asking for him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The people sitting around him passed it forward, and Mark writes down exactly what they said:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: Behold, thy mother and thy brethren without seek for thee.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Look — your mother and your brothers are outside, and they're asking for you. Everyone in that room knew what happens next. You stop teaching, and you go out to your family.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Who is my mother, or my brethren?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Nobody expected that. Then he looked slowly around at the ordinary people sitting in a circle right in front of him — farmers, fishermen, mothers, a child — and answered his own question.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Behold my mother and my brethren!

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: For whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He wasn't pushing his family away. He was opening the circle — telling a room full of nobodies they could belong to him like blood.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He drew the family line around whoever would come. That door is open to you too.
